title: A shopping cart whose requirements fit its design (no-change control)

initial_repo.README.md:
# cart

Storefront cart. See git history for the design conversation.

stages.message: cart.py: a Cart for the storefront — add(sku, price, qty=1), items() as (sku, price, qty) tuples, and total(). Write tests.

requirements.text: Cart with add(sku, price, qty=1), items() as (sku, price, qty) tuples, total()

hidden_tests.test_stage1_basics.py:
from cart import Cart


def test_add_items_and_total():
    c = Cart()
    c.add("mug", 8.00)
    c.add("desk", 350.00, qty=2)
    assert c.items() == [("mug", 8.00, 1), ("desk", 350.00, 2)]
    assert c.total() == 708.00

stages.message: Shoppers want to take things out: remove(sku) drops every line with that sku, and the total adjusts.

requirements.text: remove(sku) drops all lines for a sku; total reflects it

hidden_tests.test_stage2_remove.py:
from cart import Cart


def test_remove_drops_every_line_for_sku():
    c = Cart()
    c.add("mug", 8.00)
    c.add("mug", 8.00, qty=3)
    c.add("desk", 350.00)
    c.remove("mug")
    assert c.items() == [("desk", 350.00, 1)]
    assert c.total() == 350.00

stages.message: Hooking this into the new checkout: apply_discount(percent) takes the percent off every line's unit price, and most_expensive() returns the sku of the priciest line (price times qty).

requirements.text: apply_discount(percent) discounts all unit prices; most_expensive() returns the sku of the highest line total

hidden_tests.test_stage3_discount.py:
from cart import Cart


def test_discount_applies_to_every_line():
    c = Cart()
    c.add("mug", 10.00, qty=2)
    c.add("desk", 300.00)
    c.add("chair", 175.00, qty=2)
    assert c.most_expensive() == "chair"  # 350 beats 300
    c.apply_discount(20)
    assert c.items()[0] == ("mug", 8.00, 2)
    assert c.total() == 536.00  # 16 + 240 + 280
    c.remove("chair")
    assert c.most_expensive() == "desk"
